This article is about WTA number 1 rankings since 1975. For the all-time list, see World number 1 ranked female tennis players.

 merit-based system for determining the rankings in women's tennis. The top-ranked singles player is the player who, over the previous 52 weeks, has garnered the most ranking points on the WTA Tour. Points are awarded based on how far a player advances in tournaments and the category of those tournaments. The WTA has used a computerized system for determining the rankings since November 3, 1975. Since 1975, 29 women have been ranked No. 1 in singles by the WTA, of which 16 have been year-end No. 1.

Aryna Sabalenka is the current singles world No. 1.

The WTA rankings are the ratings defined by the Women's Tennis Association, introduced in November 1975. The computer that calculates the ranking is nicknamed "Medusa".

Aryna Sabalenka is the current world No. 1 in women's singles.

 for singles and 12 for doubles. Points are awarded based on how far a player advances in a tournament. The basis for calculating a player's ranking are those tournaments that yield the highest ranking points during the rolling 52-week period. For singles, the period must include:

 the four Grand Slams
 six WTA 1000 Mandatory combined/virtually combined tournaments
 one WTA 1000 Mandatory (WTA-only) tournament
 the best of seven results from all WTA 1000 Mandatory, WTA 500, WTA 250, and WTA 125 Tournaments and ITF W15+ events
 the WTA Finals as a bonus tournament if the player attendedFor doubles, the best 12 tournament results across all tournament levels are used. Unlike singles, there are no specific tournament level requirements and the WTA Finals are not treated as a bonus tournament, instead they are one of the 12 if applicable.

Up until 2016, the WTA also distributed ranking points, for singles players only, who competed at the Summer Olympics. However, this has since been discontinued.

In order to appear on the WTA rankings, players must earn ranking points in at least three tournaments, or a minimum of 10 singles ranking points or 10 doubles ranking points in one or more tournaments.

The points distribution for tournaments in 2024 is shown below. Points earned in 2023 and before were different and retained their values until they expired after 52 weeks except for 2013 points.

# WTA Singles World Rankings - complete list: Sabalenka hits 100 weeks at the top, Rybakina close second

Discover the top 100 women's singles players in the world right now, as the best tennis players battle for glory on the WTA Tour.

Sabalenka Wimbledon 2026

Who is the best female tennis player in the world?

Based on the numbers of the WTA singles rankings, Aryna Sabalenka remains the long-undisputed world No.1.

After rising to the top in October 2024, it has now been 100 weeks at the ranking's summit for the 28-year-old.

The 2026 Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year has won four Grand Slam titles so far, with three singles trophies this season.

Despite Sabalenka’s loss in the fourth round of Wimbledon, she managed to hold off world No.2 Elena Rybakina’s charge for top position after the latter exited one round earlier. A week after the tournament, the gap remains at 407 points.

But Rybakina has a significant, almost 2,000-point lead over those lower in the ranking.

After making the Wimbledon quarter-finals for the second time, USA's top-ranked player Jessica Pegula has climbed to the world No.3 spot she last held exactly a year prior.

Fellow USA star Coco Gauff defeated Pegula at Wimbledon and subsequently jumped three spots behind her to hold No.4.

Czech compatriots Linda Nosková and Karolína Muchová have spent much of the year trading places in the top 10, but after they shared Centre Court at the Wimbledon final, both placed in the list with career-high ranks.
